scope: Prevent ownerless ATTRIB output and add fast allocation rollback, same-codec retry, raw group proof, and typed readback for a plain ATTRIB carried by its owning INSERT across the supported DXF revisions.

source.kind: locally generated in-memory DRW_Insert and DRW_Attrib
source.profile: One INSERT with one single-line ATTRIB carrying a nondefault tag, text, insertion/alignment points, height, width scale, rotation, oblique angle, text generation, horizontal/vertical alignment, attribute flags, and field length.

implementation.guard: writeAttrib refuses output with neither an explicit ownerOverride nor an explicit source parent owner. This prevents default owner fallback from publishing a bare top-level ATTRIB. Existing ATTDEF subtype dispatch remains unchanged.
implementation.method: For each revision and encoding, first prove that ownerless writeAttrib refusal preserves the seeded destination and caller state, then switch the same adapter to write the valid owning INSERT and require byte-identical output plus raw and typed readback. Also calibrate each successful full-document write, inject std::bad_alloc at every measured allocation, require the destination and complete INSERT/ATTRIB caller state to remain unchanged, retry on the same codec and compare exact bytes, then verify raw ATTRIB fields/owner role and fresh typed INSERT/ATTRIB import readback. R12 Binary uses its one-byte group-code reader.

validation.focusedCTestLog: build-gcc/Testing/Temporary/LastTest.log records ownerless refusal and corrected same-codec INSERT retry for all 16 revision/encoding profiles, plus 350 injected-allocation rollback/retry/readback checks.

limitations: Generated transaction and same-library self-readback evidence only; producer and native application behavior remain unqualified.
One single-line ATTRIB profile is covered. ATTDEF, embedded multiline ATTRIB, retained Xrecord variants, and outer annotative payloads remain separate profiles.
This exercises ATTRIB through the owning INSERT compound route; no standalone ATTRIB-in-ENTITIES support is claimed.
An explicit owner handle is a caller assertion; it does not independently prove producer semantics or qualify an external manually assembled INSERT/TABLE sequence.
No support claim is promoted and no DWG/DXF fixture is committed.

planImpact.completedSlice: Ownerless writeAttrib output is now refused atomically. A generated one-ATTRIB attributed INSERT passes ownerless-refusal/corrected-retry controls plus ASCII/Binary allocation rollback, caller-state preservation, byte-identical retry, raw owner/field checks, and typed readback across AC1009/AC1014/AC1015/AC1018/AC1021/AC1024/AC1027/AC1032.
planImpact.remainingP6G: Continue exact public-writer inventory and uncovered overload/profile variants; this does not close producer semantics or broader ATTRIB-family support.
